I visited a man today who was in turn a teacher, mentor, and friend to me. He was a big man with the carriage of an athlete, he helped coached my school soccer team and track team. and taught several course I attended while in school.

I visited him this morning and kept a straight face while we chatted, but I couldn't drive once I left for the tears in my eyes. He taught me to think and gave me a love of learning for its own sake. Now he's about to die and still acts like nothing's happening, "just being me," he says. 18 months ago he'd pass for 40 with a little grey. Now he looks like a hundred year old with a little bone white hair. I'll never be able to remember him without seeing that reed thin man shuffling along and shaking as I said goodbye at the door.

Never visit anyone you love who may die from sickness. You'll regret it.
